[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"TensorFlow Core Concepts and Tensors"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Welcome to this technical tutorial on TensorFlow core concepts. TensorFlow is an open-source library for numerical computation and large-scale machine learning. At the heart of every TensorFlow program is the Tensor."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is a Tensor?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A tensor is a generalization of vectors and matrices to potentially higher dimensions. Internally, TensorFlow represents tensors as n-dimensional arrays of base datatypes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Rank: The dimension of a tensor. A scalar has rank 0, a vector has rank 1, and a matrix has rank 2."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Shape: The length of each dimension (axis) of the tensor."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Type: The type of data stored in the tensor (e.g., float32, int32, string)."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating Tensors in Python"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let us look at how to create basic tensors using the TensorFlow Python API. First, ensure you import TensorFlow."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import tensorflow as tf

# Creating a rank-0 tensor (scalar)
scalar = tf.constant(7)
print("Scalar:", scalar)

# Creating a rank-1 tensor (vector)
vector = tf.constant([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
print("Vector:", vector)

# Creating a rank-2 tensor (matrix)
matrix = tf.constant([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
print("Matrix:", matrix)"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Tensor Operations"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Tensors support standard mathematical operations such as addition, element-wise multiplication, and matrix multiplication."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"a = tf.constant([[1, 2],
                 [3, 4]])
b = tf.constant([[5, 6],
                 [7, 8]])

# Element-wise addition
addition = tf.add(a, b)
print("Addition:\n", addition)

# Matrix multiplication
matmul = tf.matmul(a, b)
print("Matrix Multiplication:\n", matmul)"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding tensors, their shapes, and how to perform basic operations on them provides the foundational knowledge required to build complex neural networks in TensorFlow."}]
